title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
author: United Nations General Assembly
citation: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, resolution 217 A (III), Articles 1, 2, 13, 17, 23 and 25
difficulty: Formal clauses read with matching original explainers.
why: Primary text for interpreting protections and comparing them with fictional events.
note: Official English page and alternate digital library record refused automated reads. Four articles compared with the 2017 base copies offline. Check official English wording, spelling and paragraph breaks before release. First reads of Articles 13 and 25 are reserved for days 9 and 38.

title: Copyright in United Nations Publications
author: United Nations Secretariat
why: Establishes the reproduction basis for the official resolution.
note: Paragraph 10 permits quotation of non-copyright material. Paragraph 13(a) explains the public-domain presumption for already distributed documents bearing United Nations symbols. Credit the United Nations.

title: Crop and field planning tools for vegetable farmers
author: University of Minnesota Extension
citation: Natalie Hoidal, Crop and field planning tools for vegetable farmers
why: Checks the order of harvests and the kinds of crops grown in the setting.
note: Supports early leafy crops and peas, summer beans, sweet corn and fruiting crops, later roots and squash.

title: Harvesting and storing home garden vegetables
author: University of Minnesota Extension
citation: Cindy Tong, Harvesting and storing home garden vegetables
why: Checks picking, roots, heads, pods and handling details in the novel.

title: Planting vegetables in midsummer for fall harvest
author: University of Minnesota Extension
citation: Jill MacKenzie, Planting vegetables in midsummer for fall harvest
why: Checks early greens and peas, small kale leaves, and later roots including turnips.

title: Agricultural labor standards and wage statements
author: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
citation: Wage and Hour Division, MSPA Notice of Workers' Rights
difficulty: Agricultural labor guidance for production reference.

author: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health
why: Checks water access, shade and rest when the crew works in heat.
